expectations.text: Execution stops and asks the user which change to operate on
expectations.evidence: Final reply states: "Both openspec/changes/add-farewell and openspec/changes/refactor-hello are currently active (neither is archived), so I can't tell which one you mean by \"the active change.\" Could you confirm which one to execute section 1 of?" — this is a direct stop-and-ask, and the git state confirms no code changes were made (status --porcelain empty, greetings.py unchanged, HEAD == main), consistent with execution halting pending user clarification.
expectations.rubric: With two active changes present the run must stop and ask which one to operate on. 'Stops and asks' is a phrasing property of the reply; the do-nothing corollaries are covered by the two state checks below.

expectations.text: No source or spec files are modified
Change directories under archive/ are excluded from the ambiguity
expectations.evidence: The reply enumerates exactly the two active changes 'add-farewell' and 'refactor-hello' as the source of ambiguity ('Both openspec/changes/add-farewell and openspec/changes/refactor-hello are currently active'), and does not mention the archived 'archive/2026-01-add-punctuation' directory as a candidate despite the transcript showing it was found and excluded via 'find ... -not -path */archive/*'.
expectations.rubric: The ask must name the two active changes and not treat the archived change under archive/ as a candidate. Requires reading which changes the reply enumerates.
